# Codex verification brief — relation map on the try-it page (commit bfcb83d)

You are an independent reviewer. Do NOT edit any tracked file. Write scratch files only under
`audit_evidence_claims/m1/`. Put your report in `audit_evidence_claims/m1/REPORT.md`.
End with exactly one line: `VERDICT: APPROVE` or `VERDICT: CHANGES REQUIRED`.

## What was added

`src/app.py` `Engine.explore(text, per_group=30)` and `POST /api/explore`; `web/try.html` section "0. 관계 지도"
(`drawMap`, `explore`, `itemDetail`, the GKO/TKO/ACT/PH tables, click-through and the "따라온 길" trail);
`tests/test_app.py::test_explore_draws_a_drug_and_refuses_a_biosimilar`. Run tests with
`python -m pytest tests -q -p no:cacheprovider` (317). Start the page with `python src/app.py [port]` (use a port
other than 8765, which may already be in use) and exercise it over HTTP.

The page is for a domain reviewer to look at one node (drug, target, company, investigator, trial, disease) and
everything a live edge ties it to, grouped by relation, and to click through. It is read-only.

## The guarantees claimed (page text in section 0 and the `explore` docstring)

1. Every neighbour shown is joined to the centre by a live (not retired) edge to a live node, and the group label
   states the relation and its direction correctly (e.g. "이 약의 임상을 주관한 곳 (주관 ≠ 개발)" for
   Company -SPONSORS_TRIAL_OF-> Drug seen from the drug).
2. Details shown for a neighbour are the stored values: trial phases/status/start/title/url, sponsor trial count
   (`evidence_trials`) and sponsor class, drug trial count in the graph (EVALUATES), max phase, action type.
3. A name the question linker refuses (biosimilar, distinct product, tracer) is reported as refused, never drawn
   as the originator molecule; an unknown name says "not found".
4. Groups are ordered by size and each list keeps the `per_group` neighbours with most evidence; the page says
   when a list is cut and shows the true total.
5. Nothing is written; no model is called.

## What to verify (reproduce; cite file:line and exact inputs)

A. **Wrong relations or directions.** Any centre where an edge is grouped under the wrong label or direction,
   self-loops (src == dst), edges with both ends equal to the centre, PARENT_OF/SPONSORS/STUDIES/ASSOCIATED_WITH
   direction wording, Investigator vs Company handling, nodes whose type the tables do not cover.
B. **Name resolution.** `explore` takes the first non-refused hit of `link_entities`. Inputs with several entities
   ("osimertinib EGFR"), a refused token next to a real one ("Mvasi bevacizumab"), salts vs parents, company aliases
   with `also_matching_ids` (only the first id is drawn — is that misleading?), node ids vs names that collide,
   case/whitespace/Unicode, long inputs. Is anything drawn that the input does not name, or a refused product drawn
   as the originator?
C. **Wrong values.** Trial counts, sponsor counts, max phase and action shown versus the database
   (`data/processed/oncokg.sqlite`); retired edges/nodes leaking in; counts computed over retired edges;
   the `trials` count chunking; JSON props that are null or malformed.
D. **Cutting and ordering.** Is the "most evidence" ordering what the page says (trials are ordered by start date
   string — is that what the text implies)? Does the map's subset (`drawMap` allocation) ever hide a whole group
   or misstate totals? The Disease node (thousands of neighbours) — performance and output size.
E. **Page safety and correctness.** HTML/SVG injection from labels, titles, ids, URLs (`href` with `javascript:`?),
   edge ids in `data-id` attributes, the trail/back buttons after errors, double clicks, refused/not-found states,
   dark mode legibility is not in scope.
F. **Server.** Error handling for empty/oversized input, concurrency with the lock, behaviour when the DB has
   retired rows.
G. **Docs and wording.** Section 0 text, README/README.ko lines for `app.py`, the module docstring: do they claim
   more than the code does? Korean labels in GKO/ACT/PH that misstate the stored code.

## Approval bar

No known way for the map to show a relation that is not a live edge, a wrong direction or relation wording, a
value that differs from the stored one, a refused product drawn as the originator, or script injection. Report
should-fix items (misleading wording, cut lists without notice) separately from blockers.

---
name: review
description: Review the changes since a fixed point (commit, branch, tag, or merge-base) along two axes ??Standards (does the code follow this repo's documented coding standards?) and Spec (does the code match what the originating issue/PRD asked for?). Runs both reviews in parallel sub-agents and reports them side by side. Use when the user wants to review a branch, a PR, work-in-progress changes, or asks to "review since X".
---

Two-axis review of the diff between `HEAD` and a fixed point the user supplies:

- **Standards** ??does the code conform to this repo's documented coding standards?
- **Spec** ??does the code faithfully implement the originating issue / PRD / spec?

Both axes run as **parallel sub-agents** so they don't pollute each other's context, then this skill aggregates their findings.

The issue tracker should have been provided to you ??run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` if `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` is missing.

## Process

### 1. Pin the fixed point

Whatever the user said is the fixed point ??a commit SHA, branch name, tag, `main`, `HEAD~5`, etc. If they didn't specify one, ask for it.

Capture the diff command once: `git diff <fixed-point>...HEAD` (three-dot, so the comparison is against the merge-base). Also note the list of commits via `git log <fixed-point>..HEAD --oneline`.

Before going further, confirm the fixed point resolves (`git rev-parse <fixed-point>`) and the diff is non-empty. A bad ref or empty diff should fail here ??not inside two parallel sub-agents.

### 2. Identify the spec source

Look for the originating spec, in this order:

1. Issue references in the commit messages (`#123`, `Closes #45`, GitLab `!67`, etc.) ??fetch via the workflow in `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.
2. A path the user passed as an argument.
3. A PRD/spec file under `docs/`, `specs/`, or `.scratch/` matching the branch name or feature.
4. If nothing is found, ask the user where the spec is. If they say there isn't one, the **Spec** sub-agent will skip and report "no spec available".

### 3. Identify the standards sources

Anything in the repo that documents how code should be written, such as `CODING_STANDARDS.md` or `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

### 4. Spawn both sub-agents in parallel

Send a single message with two `Agent` tool calls. Use the `general-purpose` subagent for both.

**Standards sub-agent prompt** ??include:

- The full diff command and commit list.
- The list of standards-source files you found in step 3.
- The brief: "Report ??per file/hunk where relevant ??every place the diff violates a documented standard. Cite the standard (file + the rule). Distinguish hard violations from judgement calls. Skip anything tooling enforces. Under 400 words."

**Spec sub-agent prompt** ??include:

- The diff command and commit list.
- The path or fetched contents of the spec.
- The brief: "Report: (a) requirements the spec asked for that are missing or partial; (b) behaviour in the diff that wasn't asked for (scope creep); (c) requirements that look implemented but where the implementation looks wrong. Quote the spec line for each finding. Under 400 words."

If the spec is missing, skip the Spec sub-agent and note this in the final report.

### 5. Aggregate

Present the two reports under `## Standards` and `## Spec` headings, verbatim or lightly cleaned. Do **not** merge or rerank findings ??the two axes are deliberately separate (see _Why two axes_).

End with a one-line summary: total findings per axis, and the worst issue _within each axis_ (if any). Don't pick a single winner across axes ??that's the reranking the separation exists to prevent.

## Why two axes

A change can pass one axis and fail the other:

- Code that follows every standard but implements the wrong thing ??**Standards pass, Spec fail.**
- Code that does exactly what the issue asked but breaks the project's conventions ??**Spec pass, Standards fail.**

Reporting them separately stops one axis from masking the other.

# Independent relation-map review — round 28

Reviewed **HEAD `23b07f55dcb8a0d9a3416c0f0f8d46ffc9ef0c41`**, on 2026-11-04 (Asia/Seoul). **CHANGES REQUIRED.** Three P1 identity mechanisms remain: affirmative focus wording is still negated by the label guard; common cyanine/rhodamine abbreviations evade the dye guard; and an existing ADC's blanket exemption discards an explicitly recognized extra modification. All three also occur with the previous query module, so these are inherited gaps rather than regressions introduced by the latest commit.

The exact eight strict M27 leaks are now **FIXED**. That result and **355 passing tests** do not close the broader guarantee. Fresh evidence confirms **11 cases where every recognizer misses**, plus **3 cases where joining is recognized but the ADC exemption suppresses refusal**. All 14 pass complete map and trial/sponsor QA evidence equality checks against their corresponding unmodified drug. The actual page callbacks generate the same incorrect centre SVG and trail. [Direct and HTTP assertions](attacks/assertions.json), [page assertions](contract/current_callback_assertions.json), [pytest output](checks/pytest.txt), [pytest execution](checks/pytest_summary.json).

## Method and controls

Repair notes were hypotheses, not verification. Earlier reproduction scripts were reused with recorded hashes and output/port adaptations; the history and contract tables below give **FIXED / NOT FIXED per finding**, including exact primary and supporting inputs. M2's incomplete work and completed M2b are covered; M27 uses `attacks/FINDINGS.md` because there is no completed report. User-recorded over-refusals and the two owner-curation data limitations are retained separately and do not drive the blocker verdict.

The attack comparison contains **48 current/HEAD^ pairs**. The root independently ran the **unmodified `python src/app.py` CLI** on owned port **9955**, making **200 HTTP requests for 50 inputs** across resolve, explore, and trial/sponsor ask endpoints. All returned HTTP 200; page bytes equal the worktree, the database hash is unchanged, and the port is closed. HTTP success is not semantic correctness. The two extra inputs independently confirm the historical fragmented qualifiers `b.i.o.similar bevacizumab` and `lip.osomal doxorubicin`. [HTTP capture](checks/independent_m28_http.json), [lifecycle](checks/independent_m28_lifecycle.json), [reuse manifest](checks/http_reuse_manifest.json).

All **50 actual page form callbacks** run without rendering errors and reproduce their response's centre or refusal state. This is the real page JavaScript in a **Node VM with controlled DOM/fetch**, not browser painting or browser-executed XSS. HEAD^ comparisons load only its `query.py` alongside current modules/data; they are not historical deployments. Diagnostic ablations replace helpers/globals in memory, restore them, and clear caches; they identify causes and are not proposed production patches. No application code was edited and no model was called. [Current source excerpts](checks/source_excerpts.md), [causal ablations](attacks/counterfactual.json).


## M28-B1 — focus-word repair is absent from the label guard (P1)

Exact primary: **`trastuzumab not only radiolabelled but also purified`**. This affirms radiolabelling and adds purification. Both current and previous query modules return **TRASTUZUMAB / CHEMBL1201585**, the complete bare-trastuzumab map (**13 graph trials**) and the complete bare trial/sponsor QA evidence (**12 / 12 rows**). The original CLI independently returns the same complete map and evidence arrays. Every actual refusal stage misses: no BLOCKED resolver component, `_resolver_blocked={}`, `_qualified=False`, `_item_has_isotope=False`, `_item_joined=False`, every `_marked` call returns None, `_whole_name=None`, no public or QA Refused entity. [Stage trace](attacks/new_results.json), [strict direct/HTTP assertions](attacks/assertions.json), [original CLI capture](checks/independent_m28_http.json).

`_FOCUS` is declared at `src/query.py:243-244` and used by `_item_joined` at `267`; `_item_has_isotope` at `302-305` still starts negation after every `not`. `_negated_end` at `218-219` sees `only` ending in `ly` and extends that negation onto the following strong label `radiolabelled`. The successful conjugation-focused repair therefore leaves the same affirmative semantics broken in the independent label path. `_marked` at `585-587` receives False, and `Engine.explore` at `src/app.py:88-95` draws the ordinary hit.

Seven supporting complete affirmative inputs reproduce the same strict all-stage leak: `trastuzumab not merely radiolabelled but also purified`; `trastuzumab not solely radiolabelled but also purified`; `trastuzumab not only labelled with Alexa Fluor 488 but also purified`; `trastuzumab not merely labelled with Alexa Fluor 488 but also purified`; `trastuzumab not only tagged with biotin but also purified`; `trastuzumab not simply tagged with biotin but also purified`; `trastuzumab not only radioactive but also purified`.

Controls isolate semantics: `trastuzumab only radiolabelled` correctly refuses; true negatives `trastuzumab not radiolabelled` and `trastuzumab not labelled with Alexa Fluor 488` retain TRASTUZUMAB. All seven listed focus words with positive DM1 conjugation are covered by the combined prior/new cases and correctly refuse. Adding only `and flat[i] not in _FOCUS` to the label guard **in memory** makes all eight focus-label leaks refuse, preserves the genuine negatives and ordinary controls, and leaves the dye-code and ADC-exemption leaks unchanged. The helper and caches are restored. [Exact original/replacement and causal outputs](attacks/counterfactual.json), [diagnostic script](attacks/counterfactual.py).

Identity premise does not require inferring any particular radiopharmaceutical. The affirmative input describes a labelled version and must not silently become the unlabelled drug. For the fluorescent corroborations, the manufacturer's description explicitly explains covalent attachment of Alexa Fluor dye or biotin to IgG. [Thermo Fisher antibody labeling](https://www.thermofisher.com/us/en/home/life-science/antibodies/antibody-labeling.html).

## M28-B2 — standard cyanine and rhodamine abbreviations evade the named-dye guard (P1)

Exact primary: **`trastuzumab linked to Cy3`**; equally decisive corroboration: **`trastuzumab linked to TAMRA`**. Both current and previous versions draw the complete bare TRASTUZUMAB map and **12 / 12** QA arrays. The same strict all-stage assertions as B1 pass, including `_item_joined=False`. **`trastuzumab linked to BODIPY`** is a further named-dye-family corroboration; the blocker does not depend on resolving a particular BODIPY derivative. [Stage outputs](attacks/new_results.json), [equality assertions](attacks/assertions.json).

At `src/query.py:240-242`, the code list recognizes `cy5`, `cy7`, `cy55` but omits `cy3` and `tamra`. New `_REAGENTS` entries at `248-251` recognize strings starting `cyanin` or `rhodamin`; ordinary abbreviations have neither prefix. The pieces/reagent predicate at `263-265` is therefore False, and the `linked` branch at `280-284` misses. The literal controls `trastuzumab linked to cyanine 3`, `trastuzumab linked to rhodamine`, `trastuzumab linked to Cy5.5`, and both Alexa cases refuse.

The identity premise is manufacturer-supported, not inferred from an arbitrary capitalized token: Cytiva calls Cy3 a fluorescent cyanine and provides an antibody-conjugation protocol. Thermo Fisher identifies TAMRA as a tetramethylrhodamine derivative used for protein conjugates. [Cytiva Cy3 specification](https://d3.cytivalifesciences.com/prod/IFU/28951573.pdf), [Thermo Fisher rhodamine reference](https://www.thermofisher.com/us/en/home/references/molecular-probes-the-handbook/fluorophores-and-their-amine-reactive-derivatives/long-wavelength-rhodamines-texas-red-dyes-and-qsy-quenchers.html). These sources establish dye identity and the modification interpretation; they do not establish a unique registered trastuzumab-dye product.

Adding only `cy3`, `tamra`, and `bodipy` to the existing code set in memory makes the three dye cases refuse, retains nine ordinary/negative/bare-ADC controls, and leaves the label-focus and ADC-exemption defects intact. This diagnoses vocabulary coverage; it is not a proposed complete dye dictionary. [Causal outputs](attacks/counterfactual.json).

## M28-B3 — a recognized extra dye or carrier is ignored for an existing ADC (P1)

Exact primary: **`trastuzumab emtansine linked to Alexa Fluor 488`**. The current map and both complete QA evidence arrays equal **bare trastuzumab emtansine / CHEMBL1743082**, with **5 graph trials / 5 trial QA / 5 sponsor QA rows**. **`trastuzumab deruxtecan linked to Alexa Fluor 488`** similarly equals **CHEMBL4297844**, with **6 / 6 / 4** rows. **`trastuzumab emtansine conjugated to polyethylene glycol`** independently corroborates the same exemption. All three occur on HEAD^ too. [Full direct traces](attacks/new_results.json), [strict public-stage and HTTP equality](attacks/assertions.json).

These are deliberately separated from the 11 cases whose recognizers all return False: here `_item_joined=True`, including when called only on the text outside the matched ADC name. Nevertheless **every actual refusal stage still misses**: resolver unblocked, `_marked=None`, `_whole_name=None`, public linker and QA contain no Refused object, and the map draws the existing ADC. A True internal cue is not a refusal.

`_payload_name` at `src/query.py:234-236` returns True solely because the stored preferred name contains a later `emtansine` or `deruxtecan` word. The conjunction at `590-592` then suppresses the already-detected joining cue outside that matched name. The guard exempts the existing ADC from any additional linkage. This is broader than accepting an already stored ADC name: the new Alexa label is not part of either stored ADC name. The same manufacturer antibody-label chemistry above supports distinguishing a further dye-labelled antibody from the corresponding unlabelled ADC; no unique approved or measured clinical product is asserted.

In memory, replacing only `_payload_name` with `lambda name: False` makes these three extra-modification descriptions refuse while preserving the two bare ADC names in this measured cohort. It leaves B1 and B2 intact. This isolates the broad exemption; removing it globally is **not** offered as a completeness-tested production repair. An eventual repair must still preserve authentic stored ADC names and aliases. [Literal original helper, diagnostic replacement, independent controls and restoration](attacks/counterfactual.json).

"""A local page for trying the pipeline by hand.

    python src/app.py            then open http://localhost:8765

A relation map (a node and the nodes live edges tie it to, a capped list per relation,
click to move on),
then four boxes: type an intervention string the way a registry would write it and see
how the resolver reads it, or ask a question and see the grounded answer with its
evidence, give a structured answer (claims citing evidence edges) and see which
claims the graph supports and the answer written from them, or paste free prose and
see what the auxiliary word-order check flags. All of them call
the functions the pipeline uses (resolve_drug_string, OncoKG.answer,
OncoKG.check_groundedness) on the built artefacts, so what the page shows is what the
pipeline would do. Nothing is written; the language model is never called.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sqlite3
import sys
import threading
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
import config as C
import normalize as N
import textrules as T
from query import OncoKG

PAGE = C.WEB / "try.html"
PORT = 8765


class Engine:
    def __init__(self):
        self.kg = OncoKG()
        # A browser opens spare connections it may never use, which would stall a
        # single-threaded server; requests are threaded, the engine is not.
        self.kg.conn.close()
        self.kg.conn = sqlite3.connect(C.PROCESSED / "oncokg.sqlite", check_same_thread=False)
        self.kg.conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
        self.lock = threading.Lock()
        self.dic = self.kg.dic
        self.index_keys = self.kg.index_keys
        target_rows, _, _ = N._load("targets")
        self.target_keys = N.target_guard_keys(target_rows, self.dic)

    def resolve(self, text: str) -> dict:
        out = N.resolve_drug_string(text, self.dic, self.index_keys, self.target_keys)
        for c in out["components"]:
            d = self.dic["drugs"].get(c.get("drug_id") or "")
            if d:
                c["drug"] = {k: d.get(k) for k in
                             ("name", "drug_type", "max_phase_overall", "max_phase_in_nsclc")}
                c["drug"]["mechanisms"] = [m.get("mechanismOfAction") if isinstance(m, dict) else m
                                           for m in (d.get("mechanisms") or [])][:3]
                c["drug"]["trials"] = self.kg.conn.execute(
                    "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM edge WHERE rel='EVALUATES' AND dst=? AND retired_at IS NULL",
                    (d["drug_id"],)).fetchone()[0]
                par = self.dic["drugs"].get(d.get("parent_molecule") or "")
                if par:
                    c["drug"]["parent"] = {"name": par["name"], "trials": self.kg.conn.execute(
                        "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM edge WHERE rel='EVALUATES' AND dst=? AND retired_at IS NULL",
                        (par["drug_id"],)).fetchone()[0]}
            if c.get("candidates"):
                c["candidate_names"] = [
                    (self.dic["drugs"].get(x) or {}).get("name", x) for x in c["candidates"]]
        return out

    def explore(self, text: str, per_group: int = 30) -> dict:
        """One live node and the live nodes its live edges tie it to, grouped by relation.

        `text` is a node id or a name the question linker reads as one entity. A name
        the linker refuses (a biosimilar, a reformulation, a tracer) is reported, never
        mapped to the originator. Each group keeps `per_group` neighbours, sorted as the
        page states: trials by start date (latest first), drugs by trials in the graph,
        sponsors by trials they lead, disease targets by association score. Sponsorship
        keeps its role (lead sponsor or collaborator)."""
        conn = self.kg.conn
        also: list = []
        matched = None
        row = conn.execute("SELECT id FROM node WHERE id=? AND retired_at IS NULL",
                           (text,)).fetchone()
        if row:
            nid = row["id"]
        else:
            ents = self.kg.link_entities(text)
            refused = [e for e in ents if e["type"] == "Refused"]
            hits = [e for e in ents if e.get("id") and e["type"] != "Refused"]
            if not hits:
                if refused:
                    return {"refused": refused[0]["label"], "why": refused[0]["why"]}
                return {"not_found": text}
            nid, matched = hits[0]["id"], hits[0].get("matched_alias") or hits[0].get("matched_text")
            also = [{"id": e["id"], "type": e["type"], "label": e["label"]} for e in hits[1:]]
            for oid in hits[0].get("also_matching_ids") or []:   # one alias, several ids
                lab = conn.execute("SELECT type, label FROM node WHERE id=? AND retired_at IS NULL",
                                   (oid,)).fetchone()
                if lab and oid != nid:
                    also.append({"id": oid, "type": lab["type"], "label": lab["label"]})
            # the same words may also name an organisation or a target the linker
            # passed over because a drug alias came first ("Roche" is a folic acid alias)
            key = T.canonical_key(text)
            for cid in self.kg.companies.get(key, []):
                if cid != nid and all(x.get("id") != cid for x in also):
                    lab = conn.execute("SELECT label FROM node WHERE id=? AND retired_at IS NULL",
                                       (cid,)).fetchone()
                    if lab:
                        also.append({"id": cid, "type": "Company", "label": lab["label"]})
            t = self.kg.targets.get(text.strip().lower())
            if t and t["target_id"] != nid:
                also.append({"id": t["target_id"], "type": "Target", "label": t["symbol"]})
            also += [{"refused": e["label"]} for e in refused]
        node = conn.execute("SELECT id, type, label, props FROM node WHERE id=? "
                            "AND retired_at IS NULL", (nid,)).fetchone()
        if node is None:                              # a name can outlive its node
            return {"not_found": text}
        rows = conn.execute(
            "SELECT e.id AS eid, e.rel, e.src, e.props AS eprops, n.id, n.type, n.label, "
            "n.props AS nprops FROM edge e JOIN node n "
            "ON n.id = CASE WHEN e.src=? THEN e.dst ELSE e.src END "
            "WHERE (e.src=? OR e.dst=?) AND e.retired_at IS NULL AND n.retired_at IS NULL",
            (nid, nid, nid)).fetchall()
        drug_ids = list({r["id"] for r in rows if r["type"] == "Drug"} | {nid})
        trials = {}
        for i in range(0, len(drug_ids), 500):
            chunk = drug_ids[i:i + 500]
            trials.update(conn.execute(               # live trials only
                "SELECT e.dst, COUNT(*) FROM edge e JOIN node t ON t.id = e.src "
                "WHERE e.rel='EVALUATES' AND e.retired_at IS NULL AND t.retired_at IS NULL "
                f"AND e.dst IN ({','.join('?' * len(chunk))}) GROUP BY e.dst", chunk).fetchall())
        groups: dict = {}
        for r in rows:
            ep, np_ = _obj(r["eprops"]), _obj(r["nprops"])
            item = {"id": r["id"], "type": r["type"], "label": r["label"], "edge_id": r["eid"]}
            role = ep.get("role") if r["rel"] == "SPONSORS" else None
            if r["type"] == "Drug":
                item["trials"] = trials.get(r["id"], 0)
                item["max_phase"] = np_.get("max_phase_overall")
            if r["rel"] == "SPONSORS_TRIAL_OF":
                n = ep.get("evidence_trials")
                # a count the edge does not record stays unknown; 0 is only for sorting
                item["evidence_trials"] = n if _number(n) else None
                item["weight"] = n if _number(n) else 0
                item["sponsor_class"] = ep.get("sponsor_class")
            elif r["type"] == "Trial":
                item.update({k: np_.get(k) for k in ("phases", "status", "title", "start_date", "url")})
                item["weight"] = str(np_.get("start_date") or "")
            elif r["type"] == "Drug":
                item["weight"] = item["trials"]
            elif r["rel"] == "ASSOCIATED_WITH":
                score = ep.get("association_score")
                item["score"] = score if _number(score) else None
                item["weight"] = item["score"] or 0
            else:
                item["weight"] = 0
            if r["rel"] == "ACTS_ON":
                item["action"] = ep.get("action_type")
            if role:
                item["role"] = role
            key = (r["rel"], "out" if r["src"] == nid else "in", r["type"], role)
            groups.setdefault(key, []).append(item)
        out = []
        for (rel, direction, ntype, role), items in groups.items():
            items.sort(key=lambda x: x["label"] or "")              # names A to Z
            items.sort(key=lambda x: x["weight"], reverse=True)     # then by the stated weight
            out.append({"rel": rel, "dir": direction, "type": ntype, "role": role,
                        "total": len(items), "items": items[:per_group]})
        out.sort(key=lambda g: -g["total"])
        props = _obj(node["props"])
        return {"center": {"id": node["id"], "type": node["type"], "label": node["label"],
                           "matched_text": matched,
                           "trials": trials.get(node["id"], 0) if node["type"] == "Drug" else None,
                           "props": {k: props.get(k) for k in
                                     ("max_phase_overall", "drug_type", "phases", "status",
                                      "title", "url", "start_date") if props.get(k) is not None}},
                "also": also, "groups": out}

    def ask(self, question: str) -> dict:
        return self.kg.answer(question, use_llm=False).to_dict()

    def structured(self, question: str, payload: str) -> dict:
        """Check a structured answer (claims citing edges) and write the answer from it."""
        kg = self.kg
        entities = kg.link_entities(question)
        evidence = kg.retrieve(kg.classify(question, entities), entities)
        res = kg.verify_structured(payload, evidence)
        res["evidence"] = [{"edge_id": e.edge_id, "statement": e.statement} for e in evidence]
        return res

    def check(self, question: str, answer: str) -> dict:
        """Check an answer someone else wrote against the evidence for the question."""
        kg = self.kg
        entities = kg.link_entities(question)
        intent = kg.classify(question, entities)
        evidence = kg.retrieve(intent, entities)
        checks = kg.check_groundedness(answer, evidence, entities, generated=True,
                                       vocabulary=set(self.dic["index"]),
                                       linker=kg.link_entities)
        return {"intent": intent, "entities": entities, "checks": checks,
                "evidence": [{"statement": e.statement, "source_record": e.source_record,
                              "source": e.source, "url": e.url} for e in evidence[:8]],
                "evidence_count": len(evidence)}


def _number(v) -> bool:
    return isinstance(v, (int, float)) and not isinstance(v, bool) and v == v


def _obj(raw) -> dict:
    """Stored props as a dict; anything else (null, a list, broken JSON) as empty."""
    try:
        v = json.loads(raw) if raw else {}
    except ValueError:
        return {}
    return v if isinstance(v, dict) else {}


def make_handler(engine: Engine):
    class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
        def _send(self, code: int, body: bytes, ctype: str):
            self.send_response(code)
            self.send_header("Content-Type", ctype)
            self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
            self.end_headers()
            self.wfile.write(body)

        def do_GET(self):
            if self.path in ("/", "/index.html"):
"""The try-it page calls the pipeline's own functions; these pin what it shows."""
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "src"))
import config as C

if not (C.PROCESSED / "oncokg.sqlite").exists():
    pytest.skip("built graph missing - run src/run_all.py first", allow_module_level=True)

import app

ENGINE = app.Engine()


def tiers(text):
    return [c["tier"] for c in ENGINE.resolve(text)["components"]]


def test_resolve_matches_pipeline_rules():
    assert tiers("placebo plus docetaxel") == ["BLOCKED_PLACEBO", "EXACT"]
    assert tiers("Mvasi") == ["BLOCKED_DISTINCT_PRODUCT"]
    assert tiers("EGFR") == ["BLOCKED_TARGET_TERM"]


def test_salt_record_reports_parent_molecule():
    drug = ENGINE.resolve("Tarceva")["components"][0]["drug"]
    assert drug["parent"]["name"] == "ERLOTINIB"


def test_check_flags_invented_name_and_number_not_relation():
    bad = ENGINE.check("Which drugs act on ALK?", "Alectinib and zorbatinib act on ALK.")
    assert {u["value"].lower() for u in bad["checks"]["unsupported_claims"]} == {"zorbatinib"}
    num = ENGINE.check("What trials evaluate Tagrisso?", "It is in 4,812 trials.")
    assert not num["checks"]["grounded"]
    # a false statement built from true tokens is caught by the claim check
    rel = ENGINE.check("Which companies are developing osimertinib?",
                       "AstraZeneca has discontinued osimertinib.")
    assert rel["checks"]["grounded"] is False


def test_explore_draws_a_drug_and_refuses_a_biosimilar():
    import app
    e = app.Engine()
    r = e.explore("osimertinib")
    assert r["center"]["id"] == "CHEMBL3353410"
    rels = {(g["rel"], g["dir"]) for g in r["groups"]}
    assert ("ACTS_ON", "out") in rels and ("SPONSORS_TRIAL_OF", "in") in rels
    assert all(len(g["items"]) <= 30 for g in r["groups"])
    assert e.explore("Mvasi").get("refused")
    assert e.explore("no such thing zz").get("not_found")

    e = app.Engine()
    r = e.explore("NCT00200395")
    roles = {(g["type"], g["role"]): [i["id"] for i in g["items"]]
             for g in r["groups"] if g["rel"] == "SPONSORS"}

    assert "ORG:genentech" not in roles.get(("Company", "lead_sponsor"), [])

def test_explore_does_not_draw_a_retired_centre_by_name():

The unresolved residue in the resolver does not stop `Engine.explore` from drawing the accepted antibody (`src/app.py:88-95`). Reversing the first two names (`ATTO 647N linked to trastuzumab`, `Cy3B linked to trastuzumab`) and removing the ATTO space (`trastuzumab linked to ATTO647N`) gives the same strict result in direct traces: **eight all-recognizer-miss cases** total.

The new predicate at `src/query.py:255-261` accepts a complete `(cy|atto|dy|af)` plus 1–4 digits and nothing following those digits. `atto647n`, `cy3b` and `dy647p1` therefore fail despite belonging to the newly handled families. Neither CF488A nor Pacific Blue is in the adjacent named-dye/word lists (`243-252`). `_item_joined` then misses the `linked` description because `reagent=False` (`276-296`). Literal controls `trastuzumab linked to ATTO 647`, `... Cy3`, and `... DY-647` refuse; explicit `trastuzumab conjugated to ATTO 647N` also refuses via the stronger joining word. The ATTO 647 control is a parser contrast, not a claim that it is interchangeable with the chemically distinct ATTO 647N dye.

These names are established dye identifiers, not invented drug-code suffixes. Merck provides an ATTO 647N protein/antibody labelling protocol; the original Cy3B study characterizes the dye and its antibody conjugate; Dyomics lists DY-647P1 for protein labelling. [Merck product document](https://www.merckmillipore.com/deepweb/assets/sigmaaldrich/product/documents/210/596/18373dat.pdf), [Cooper et al., 2004](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15615040/), [Dyomics DY-647P1](https://dyomics.com/en/products/red-excitation/dy-647p1). Manufacturer pages also document CF488A and Pacific Blue antibody labels. [Biotium](https://biotium.com/product/mix-n-stain-cf-dye-antibody-labeling-kit/?attribute_pa_conjugation=cf488a), [Thermo Fisher](https://www.thermofisher.com/order/catalog/product/tw/en/P30013). These sources establish the described modification, not a unique approved trastuzumab-dye product or its clinical evidence.

Adding only the five exact canonical dye names to `_names_reagent` **in memory** makes all eight plain-antibody cases refuse, including their QA evidence. Ordinary negative/clinical controls remain unchanged. It also repairs the extra-dye ADC examples below, confirming the shared vocabulary contribution. This finite diagnostic is not proposed as a complete production dye dictionary. [Literal original/helper replacements and causal results](counterfactual.json), [executable diagnostic](counterfactual.py).

## M29-B2 — recognized extra conjugation is still waived for a named ADC when its partner is outside the reagent vocabulary (P1)

Exact primary: **`trastuzumab emtansine conjugated to streptavidin`**. It draws **TRASTUZUMAB EMTANSINE / CHEMBL1743082**, with the exact unmodified ADC map and QA evidence (**5 graph trials / 5 trial QA / 5 sponsor QA rows**). Additional cases **`trastuzumab emtansine conjugated to ATTO 647N`** (**5 / 5 / 5**) and **`trastuzumab deruxtecan conjugated to Cy3B`** (**CHEMBL4297844; 6 / 6 / 4**) confirm the same path. All three have strict direct and original-CLI HTTP equality. [Assertions](assertions.json), [HTTP](../checks/independent_new_http.json).

Here the text outside the matched ADC name has **`_item_joined=True`**, while **`_item_reagent=False`** and **`_payload_name=True`**. The new conjunction at `src/query.py:604-610` therefore still skips refusal. Every actual refusal stage nevertheless misses exactly as in B1: no blocked resolver component, no marked refusal, no public/QA refusal. A positive internal cue is not itself a refusal. The words `conjugated to streptavidin` name an additional protein attachment; they do not describe the ADC's own emtansine payload. Bio-Rad explicitly describes coupling streptavidin to antibodies/proteins. [Bio-Rad conjugation kit](https://www.bio-rad-antibodies.com/kit/streptavidin-conjugation-kit-lnk16.html).

Controls isolate the exception. **`trastuzumab conjugated to streptavidin`** refuses, while adding **`emtansine`** makes the further-modified product accepted. Current `trastuzumab emtansine conjugated to biotin`, `... conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488`, and `... conjugated to polyethylene glycol` refuse. Bare emtansine/deruxtecan and their ordinary `antibody-drug conjugate` descriptions remain accepted.

Adding only `streptavidin` to reagent recognition in memory repairs the primary while leaving the plain-antibody dye failures unchanged. Removing the payload-name exemption entirely also repairs these three positive-join failures, **but breaks both ordinary ADC-description controls**. The latter is a causal ablation, not a production repair recommendation. All globals/caches are restored, and a fresh restored run equals the entire baseline. [Counterfactual results](counterfactual.json), [restoration and control assertions](assertions.json).

`trastuzumab emtansine linked to ATTO 647N` also leaks, but differs: the outside-name joining cue is False, although the whole-item cue is True because it includes the ADC's own `emtansine` token. It is recorded as **shared B1 vocabulary coverage on an ADC**, not misreported as a positive outside-name join exemption or counted as a third independent finding.

def post(endpoint, text):
    req = urllib.request.Request(BASE + "/api/" + endpoint,
        data=json.dumps({"text": text}).encode(),
        headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})
    start = time.perf_counter()
    try:
        response = urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30)
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as error:
        response = error
    with response:
        return {"endpoint": endpoint, "input": text, "status": response.status,
                "seconds": time.perf_counter() - start,
                "response": json.loads(response.read())}

_LABELLED = {"labelled", "labeled", "labelling", "labeling", "tagged"}
# A word just before the label that says the opposite ("non-radio-labelled")
_NOT_WORDS = {"non", "not", "no", "un", "without"}
# Symbols that are also everyday abbreviations: read beside a mass only inside one word
_SPACED_NOT = {"cr", "co", "se", "la"}
# Words that say the substance carries a radioactive label.
_LABEL_WORDS = {"tritiated", "tritium", "radiotracer", "radiotracers", "radioligand", "radionuclide",
                "radioconjugate", "radioimmunoconjugate", "radiopharmaceutical", "radioactive",
                "radiolabelled", "radiolabeled", "radiolabel"}

def _strong_label(x: str) -> bool:
    return x in _LABEL_WORDS or x in _LABELLED or x.startswith(_LABEL_STEMS)


def _negated_end(flat: list, i: int) -> int:
    """The end of the label a negation just before flat[i] governs: the shortest glued run
    that is a known label ("non-labelled", "non-radio-labelled"), a bare "radio" with the
    word it prefixes ("non-radio-astatinated"), and a label after its adverb ("not
    radioactively labelled"); never a separate later label ("non-labelled radiolabelled")."""
    end = i + 1
    for j in range(i + 1, min(len(flat), i + 3) + 1):
        if _strong_label("".join(flat[i:j])):
            end = j
            break
    else:
        if flat[i] == "radio" and i + 1 < len(flat):
            end = i + 2
    if flat[end - 1].endswith("ly") and end < len(flat) and _strong_label(flat[end]):
        end += 1
    return end


# Words that say the drug is joined to something else (a dye, a payload): a distinct
# product ("trastuzumab conjugated to DM1", "IRDye800CW-conjugated trastuzumab")
_JOINED = ("conjugat", "covalently", "bioconjugat", "immunoconjugat", "coupled", "coupling",
           "attached", "tethered", "crosslinked", "chemically")
# Payload words that mark a drug's own name as a conjugate (TRASTUZUMAB EMTANSINE,
# ETIRINOTECAN PEGOL): a later word of a several-word name, never the molecule itself
# (IRINOTECAN, TOPOTECAN, TASIDOTIN carry the same letters but are plain molecules)
_PAYLOAD = re.compile(r"\w*(tansine|tecan|dotin|ozogamicin|tesirine|duocarmazine|pegol|"
                      r"sudotox|aritox|pasudotox)|conjugate", re.I)


def _payload_name(name: str) -> bool:
    words = re.findall(r"[A-Za-z0-9]+", name or "")
    return any(_PAYLOAD.fullmatch(w) for w in words[1:]) or "conjugate" in name.lower()


# Payload, dye, carrier and chelator codes ("DM1", "MMAE", "SN-38", "PEG", "DOTA", "FITC")
_PAYLOAD_CODES = {"dm1", "dm4", "mmae", "mmaf", "sn38", "dxd", "pbd", "peg", "dota", "nota",
                  "dfo", "dtpa", "fitc", "cy5", "cy7", "cy55", "mcc", "smcc", "vcmmae", "calicheamicin",
                  "emtansine", "mertansine", "deruxtecan", "vedotin", "biotin", "hrp", "gfp"}
# "not only", "not merely": a focus, not a negation ("not only conjugated ... but also purified")
_FOCUS = {"only", "merely", "solely", "exclusively", "just", "simply", "purely"}
# Named dye families ("Alexa Fluor 488", "TAMRA", "BODIPY", "DyLight 650", "Texas Red")
_DYE_STEMS = ("irdye", "alexa", "dylight", "bodipy", "tamra", "tritc", "texasred", "fluorescein",
              "phycoerythrin", "allophycocyanin", "sulfocy", "quantumdot", "qdot",
              "pacificblue", "pacificorange", "oregongreen", "cascadeblue", "brilliantviolet",
              "streptavidin", "avidin", "neutravidin")
# Prefix pieces a negation carries through ("non-radio-immuno-conjugated")
_PIECES = {"radio", "immuno", "bio", "chemo", "photo", "nano"}
# Nouns that name what a drug is joined to ("linked to polyethylene glycol")
_REAGENTS = ("polyethylene", "glycol", "peg", "payload", "toxin", "dye", "fluoro", "fluoresc",
             "chelat", "polymer", "rhodamin", "cyanin", "nanoparticle", "liposom", "albumin", "biotin", "maytansin",
             "auristatin", "peptide", "linker", "cytotox",
             "radionuclid", "isotop", "dextran", "dendrimer", "micelle", "lipid")


def _names_reagent(flat: list) -> bool:
    """Does the text name a payload, dye, carrier or chelator? Each word, and each
    neighbouring pair glued, so a hyphenated code counts ("SN-38", "DM-1", "Texas Red")."""
    pieces = flat + [a + b for a, b in zip(flat, flat[1:])]
    return any(x.startswith(_REAGENTS) or x in _PAYLOAD_CODES or x.startswith(_DYE_STEMS)
               or re.fullmatch(r"(cy|atto|dy|af|cf|bv|alexa|alexafluor)\d{1,4}[a-z0-9]{0,3}", x)
               for x in pieces)


# What may stand beside a conjugate's own name without describing a further modification
_ADC_WORDS = {"antibody", "drug", "conjugate", "conjugates", "adc", "adcs", "immunoconjugate",
              "a", "an", "the", "is", "as", "this", "of", "and", "or"}


@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=4096)
def _beyond_adc_words(words: tuple) -> bool:
    """A named conjugate with a joining word beside it: fine for "antibody-drug conjugate",
    a further modification for anything else ("... conjugated to ATTO 647N", "... to
    streptavidin") — the partner need not be a known reagent."""
    return any(x.lower() not in _ADC_WORDS for x in _alnum_words(" ".join(words)))


@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=4096)
def _item_reagent(words: tuple) -> bool:
    return _names_reagent([x.lower() for x in _alnum_words(" ".join(words))])


@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=4096)
def _item_joined(words: tuple) -> bool:
    """Does this list item say the drug is conjugated or covalently linked to something?"""
    raw = _alnum_words(" ".join(words))
    flat = [x.lower() for x in raw]
    negated: set = set()
    # what the drug would be joined to, anywhere in the item and in either order
    # ("linked to a derivative of the toxin DM1", "polyethylene glycol linked to irinotecan")
    # each word, and each neighbouring pair glued, so a hyphenated code counts ("SN-38", "DM-1")
    reagent = _names_reagent(flat)
    for i, x in enumerate(flat):
        if i and flat[i - 1] in _NOT_WORDS and x not in _FOCUS:
            # "not only / merely / solely ... but also" affirms; otherwise the negation covers the one word it negates, carried on through an adverb
            # or a prefix piece ("not covalently linked", "non-radio-immuno-conjugated"),
            # never across to a separate affirmative ("not radiolabelled but conjugated")
            j = i
            negated.add(j)
            while j + 1 < len(flat) and (flat[j].endswith("ly") or flat[j] in _PIECES):
                j += 1
                negated.add(j)
        if i in negated:
            continue
        if x.startswith(_JOINED):
            return True
        if x == "linked":
            # "linked via a linker to", or "linked" with a payload, dye or carrier named in
            # the item; not a relation in words ("osimertinib linked to longer PFS")
            if "via" in flat[i + 1:i + 4] or reagent:
                return True
    return False


@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=4096)
def _item_has_isotope(words: tuple) -> bool:
    """Is a medical isotope written anywhere in this list item? Worked out once per item.

    Two-letter elements are read across words ("trastuzumab Ga 68"); a one-letter element
    only inside one word, mass first ("3hvinblastine") or element first ("I-124-labelled"),
    so "13 NSCLC" is not N-13 and "BKM120" is not M-120."""
    if _medical_isotope_in(T.canonical_key(" ".join(words)), one_letter=False):
        return True
    flat = [x.lower() for x in _alnum_words(" ".join(words))]
    # each word, and two or three neighbouring words glued ("radio-labelled",
    # "radio-immuno-conjugate"), unless a negation stands just before ("non-radio-labelled")
    negated: set = set()                     # the up-to-three words a negation governs
    for i in range(len(flat)):
        if i and flat[i - 1] in _NOT_WORDS and flat[i] not in _FOCUS:
            negated.update(range(i, _negated_end(flat, i)))
        if i in negated:
            continue
        for j in range(i + 1, min(len(flat), i + 3) + 1):
            x = "".join(flat[i:j])
            if x in _LABEL_WORDS or x.startswith(_LABEL_STEMS):
                return True                  # "radiolabelled", "tritiated", "radiotracer"
        if flat[i] in _LABELLED:
            return True
        if flat[i].startswith("radio"):
            runs = ["".join(flat[i:j]) for j in range(i + 1, min(len(flat), i + 3) + 1)]
            if not any(r.startswith(_RADIO_SAFE) for r in runs):
                return True                  # "radioastatinated", "radio-fluorinated"

    def named(name: str, num: str, apart: bool = False) -> bool:
        el = _ELEMENT_NAMES.get(name)
        if el is None and len(name) == 2 and name in _NAME_MASS:
            # a two-letter symbol counts as written ("Ce-134", "[134Ce]"); across a space
            # only when it is not also a common abbreviation ("CR 51" = complete response)
        if not hasattr(self, "_drug_keys"):
            self._drug_keys: dict = {}
            for k, hits in self.dic["index"].items():
                for h in hits:
                    self._drug_keys.setdefault(h["drug_id"], set()).add(k)
        return self._drug_keys.get(did, set())

    def _marked(self, key: str, did: str, tokens, seg, a: int, b: int):
        """The text that makes this drug name a distinct product or a tracer, if any.

        Checked on the same letters-and-digits form the name was looked up by: a known
        biosimilar suffix at the end of the name ("bevacizumab awwb", "bevacizumab_awwb")
        or as the next word, or an isotope label just before or after it ("[89.Zr]
        trastuzumab", "89:Zr trastuzumab")."""
        for sfx in T.BIOSIMILAR_FDA_SUFFIXES:
            stem = key[:-len(sfx)]
            if key.endswith(sfx) and stem and any(
                    h["drug_id"] == did for h in self.dic["index"].get(stem, [])):
                return " ".join(tokens[a:b])
        same = [k for k in range(len(tokens)) if seg[k] == seg[a]]
        before = [k for k in same if k < a]
        after = [k for k in same if k >= b]
        # words counted after normalisation, so punctuation never uses up the budget
        prev = _alnum_words(" ".join(tokens[k] for k in before))[-2:]
        nxt = _alnum_words(" ".join(tokens[k] for k in after))[:2]
        own = _alnum_words(" ".join(tokens[a:b]))
        lone = not before and not after      # the name is the whole list item
        # an isotope label anywhere in the name ("A33 124i"), or just before or after it
        # ("[89.Zr] trastuzumab", "trastuzumab 89 - Zr"); an isotope-shaped name counts
        # as a name only when it stands alone ("566C", "18f"), never as the substance
        # of a longer phrase ("18F fluorothymidine")
        inside = [own[i:j] for i in range(len(own)) for j in (i + 1, i + 2) if j <= len(own)]
        # and every run of the name's words glued as the key glues them, so a symbol
        # split by punctuation inside a stored alias is still an isotope ("[89Z.r]-DFO-")
        for i in range(len(own)):
            for j in range(i + 1, len(own) + 1):
                glued = "".join(own[i:j])
                if len(glued) > 6:
                    break
                if j - i > 1:
                    inside.append([glued])
        if lone and T.is_isotope_label("".join(own)):
            inside = []                      # the whole item is one isotope-shaped name
        name = " ".join(tokens[a:b])
        # the neighbours glued back together the way the lookup key glues them, so a
        # suffix or an isotope spelt in pieces is still seen ("a - w w b", "[89Z.r]")
        nxt_all = _alnum_words(" ".join(tokens[k] for k in after))[:8]
        prev_all = _alnum_words(" ".join(tokens[k] for k in before))[-8:]
        for n in range(1, len(nxt_all) + 1):
            glued = "".join(nxt_all[:n]).lower()
            if glued in T.BIOSIMILAR_FDA_SUFFIXES or T.is_isotope_label(glued):
                return f"{name} ({' '.join(nxt_all[:n])})"
            if len(glued) > 6:
                break
        for n in range(1, len(prev_all) + 1):
            glued = "".join(prev_all[-n:]).lower()
            if T.is_isotope_label(glued):
                return f"({' '.join(prev_all[-n:])}) {name}"
            if len(glued) > 6:
                break
        # a label fused to a neighbouring word, such as a chelator ("DFO89Zr", "89ZrDFO")
        for w in nxt_all[:2] + prev_all[-2:]:
            if _isotope_edge(w):
                return f"{name} ({w})"
        for ws in inside + [prev[-1:], prev, nxt[:1], nxt]:
            if ws and T.is_isotope_label(" ".join(ws)):
                return name if ws in inside else f"{name} ({' '.join(ws)})"
        # an isotope glued to the name itself ("89zr-trastuzumab" read through "[89Z.r]")
        # anything may sit between them (a chelator: "89ZrDFO-daratumumab"), so the rest
        # needs only to end, or start, with a name of the same drug
        # A medical isotope anywhere in the list item once its letters and digits are run
        # together, however it is split or cased ("89-ZrDFO trastuzumab", "3hvinblastine",
        # "trastuzumab Ga68"), refuses an unlabelled drug. A drug whose own name carries a
        # label (LUTETIUM LU 177 DOTATATE, FLUDEOXYGLUCOSE F 18) is the labelled product.
        if (_item_has_isotope(tuple(tokens[k] for k in same))
                and not _labelled(self.dic["drugs"][did]["name"])):
            return name
        # a joining word inside the matched name is the conjugate's own name
        # ("cbr96 - doxorubicin immunoconjugate"), so only the rest of the item counts
        # a drug whose own name is the conjugate (TRASTUZUMAB EMTANSINE) keeps "antibody-drug
        # conjugate", but not a further dye or carrier named beside it ("... linked to Alexa
        # Fluor 488", "... conjugated to polyethylene glycol")
        rest = tuple(tokens[k] for k in same if not a <= k < b)
        if _item_joined(rest) and (not _payload_name(self.dic["drugs"][did]["name"])
                                   or _item_reagent(rest) or _beyond_adc_words(rest)):
            return name
        # A one-letter element is left to the case-marked word check above: lower-case
        # chemistry ("13-cis retinoic acid") is not carbon-13.
        # The drug's name may sit anywhere in the rest ("89Zrpanitumumab-PET-CT"). A
        # one-letter element counts where it is written upper-case in the name
        # ("3HVINBLASTINE", "A33124I"); lower-case chemistry ("13-cis") does not.
        names = [k for k in self._keys_of(did) if len(k) >= 5]
        orig = "".join(re.findall(r"[A-Za-z0-9]+", _plain(" ".join(tokens[a:b]))))
        if len(orig) != len(key):
            orig = key.upper()                   # cannot align: treat as marked
        for i in range(2, min(6, len(key))):
            for lab, tail, at in ((key[:i], key[i:], i - 1), (key[-i:], key[:-i], len(key) - 1)):
                if not tail or not T.is_isotope_label(lab):
                    continue
                elem = re.sub(r"^\d+m?", "", lab)
                if len(elem) == 1 and not orig[at].isupper():
                    continue
                if any(k in tail for k in names):
                    return name
                # a label closing a stored name of this drug ("A33124I"): the name itself
                # is the labelled product. Only a mass used in medicine counts here, so a
                # development code's salt letter ("NSC-118218H", "DX-8951F") is not a label
                if (lab == key[-i:] and len(tail) >= 2 and key in self._keys_of(did)
                        and _medical_isotope(lab)):
                    return name

        return None

    def _whole_name(self, text: str, blocked: dict, found: list):
        """The whole input is exactly one stored drug name, letter for letter ("CP-358,774",
        "(E/Z)-AFATINIB"): read it whole rather than as the list its punctuation suggests.

        Only after every refusal has had its say: nothing the resolver or the list
        linker refused, and no product or tracer pattern in the name."""
        if blocked or any(e["type"] == "Refused" for e in found):
            return None
        name = text.strip(" ?!.")
        if T.is_distinct_product(name) or T.is_radiotracer(name):
            return None             # the list linker above has already applied the rest
        key = T.canonical_key(name)
        exact = [h for h in (self.dic["index"].get(key) or [])
                 if _fold(h["alias"]).strip(" ?!.").lower() == name.lower()]
        if not exact or len({h["drug_id"] for h in exact}) != 1:
            return None
        did = exact[0]["drug_id"]
        return {"type": "Drug", "id": did, "label": self.dic["drugs"][did]["name"],
                "matched_text": name, "matched_alias": exact[0]["alias"]}

    def _link(self, question: str) -> list[dict]:
        found: list[dict] = []
        seen: set = set()
        tokens: list[str] = []
        clause: list[int] = []          # which list piece each token is in
        inner: list[bool] = []          # token inside parentheses
        ci, depth = 0, 0
        for piece in re.split(r"[,;\uff0c\uff1b\u3001]", question):
            for raw in re.split(r"\s+", piece):
                # a slash or bar, glued or free, ends the piece ("bevacizumab - awwb/
                # osimertinib"); it must not hide a product suffix from the guards
                for j, part in enumerate(re.split(r"[/|]", raw)):
                    if j:
                        ci += 1
                    if not part:
                        continue
                    if re.search(r"\w", part):
                        # edge punctuation and wrappers off ("bevacizumab-awwb?",
                        # "(bevacizumab-awwb)"); an isotope ("[89Zr]") is checked as a word
                        t = re.sub(r"^[^\w]+|[^\w]+$", "", part)
                    elif part in ("-", "\u2013", "\u2014", "+", "&"):
                        t = part            # "bevacizumab - awwb" needs its dash
                    else:
                        t = ""
                    if t:
                        tokens.append(t)
                        clause.append(ci)
                        inner.append(depth > 0 or part.startswith("("))

    if not file.is_file() or hashlib.sha256(file.read_bytes()).hexdigest()!=digest:
        changed.append(p)
head=subprocess.check_output(['git','rev-parse','HEAD'],cwd=ROOT,text=True).strip()
diff=subprocess.run(['git','diff','--exit-code','HEAD','--'],cwd=ROOT,capture_output=True,text=True)
status=subprocess.run(['git','status','--short'],cwd=ROOT,capture_output=True,text=True)
database=hashlib.sha256((ROOT/'data/processed/oncokg.sqlite').read_bytes()).hexdigest()

report=(ROUND/'REPORT.md').read_text(encoding='utf8')
links=[]
for target in re.findall(r'\]\(([^\s)]+)\)',report):
    if re.match(r'^(?:[a-z]+:|/|#)',target): continue
    clean=target.split('#')[0]
    links.append({'target':target,'exists':(ROUND/clean).exists()})

lifecycles=[]
for file in ROUND.rglob('*lifecycle.json'):
    if 'contended' in file.parts: continue
    value=json.loads(file.read_text(encoding='utf8'))
    entry={'file':str(file.relative_to(ROUND)).replace('\\','/'),'data':value}
    if isinstance(value,dict) and isinstance(value.get('port'),int):
        with socket.socket() as sock:
            sock.settimeout(.25)
            entry['currently_closed']=sock.connect_ex(('127.0.0.1',value['port']))!=0
    lifecycles.append(entry)

result={'head_before':before['head'],'head_after':head,
        'tracked_file_count':len(before['tracked']),'changed_tracked_files':changed,
        'git_diff_exit_code':diff.returncode,'git_diff':diff.stdout,'git_status':status.stdout,
        'git_warnings':status.stderr,'database_sha256':database,
        'database_unchanged':database==before['database'],
        'report_links_checked':len(links),'missing_report_links':[x for x in links if not x['exists']],
        'lifecycles':lifecycles,
        'report_last_line':report.rstrip().splitlines()[-1]}
(OUT/'integrity_final.json').write_text(json.dumps(result,ensure_ascii=False,indent=2),encoding='utf8')
# The report links to this verification artifact itself. Recheck after writing it,
# so a first run in a clean round directory does not report its own output missing.
result['missing_report_links']=[x for x in links if not (ROUND/x['target'].split('#')[0]).exists()]
(OUT/'integrity_final.json').write_text(json.dumps(result,ensure_ascii=False,indent=2),encoding='utf8')
print(json.dumps({k:v for k,v in result.items() if k not in ['lifecycles','git_warnings']},ensure_ascii=False,indent=2))
assert not changed and head==before['head'] and diff.returncode==0 and result['database_unchanged']
assert not result['missing_report_links']
assert all(x.get('currently_closed',True) for x in lifecycles)
assert result['report_last_line'] in ('VERDICT: CHANGES REQUIRED', 'VERDICT: APPROVE')

+"""Root review of raw CLI responses, independent of attack-lane computed booleans."""
+from pathlib import Path
+import json
+OUT=Path(__file__).resolve().parent
+ROOT=OUT.parents[2]
+read=lambda p:json.loads(p.read_text(encoding='utf8'))
+http=read(OUT/'independent_new_http.json')+read(OUT/'supplementary_http.json')
+by={(r['endpoint'],r['input']):r for r in http}
+def get(endpoint,text):
+    r=by[endpoint,text]
+    assert r['status']==200
+    return r['response']
+def refusals(qa):return [x for x in qa['entities'] if x['type']=='Refused']
+new=read(OUT.parent/'attacks/assertions.json')
+direct={r['text']:r for r in read(OUT.parent/'attacks/new_results.json')['cases']}
+rows=[]
+for declared in new['leaks']:
+    t,base=declared['text'],declared['control']
+    full=get('explore',t);canonical=get('explore',base)
+    checks={'map_equals_bare':full==canonical,
+            'resolver_no_BLOCKED':all(not c['tier'].startswith('BLOCKED') for c in get('resolve',t)['components']),
+            'map_equals_direct':full==direct[t]['current']['map'],
+            'no_map_refusal':'refused' not in full}
+    for kind,question in [('trial','Which trials evaluate {}?'),('sponsor','Who sponsors trials of {}?')]:
+        qa=get('ask',question.format(t));bare=get('ask',question.format(base))
+        checks[kind+'_full_evidence_equals_bare']=qa['evidence']==bare['evidence']
+        checks[kind+'_no_refused']=not refusals(qa)
+    assert all(checks.values()),(t,checks)
+    rows.append({'text':t,'control':base,'checks':checks,'center':full['center']})
+original=read(ROOT/'audit_evidence_claims/m29/attacks/assertions.json')
+repairs=[]
+for old in original['leaks']:
+    t=old['text'];m=get('explore',t)
+    checks={'refused':bool(m.get('refused')),'no_center':'center' not in m}
+    for kind,q in [('trial','Which trials evaluate {}?'),('sponsor','Who sponsors trials of {}?')]:
+        qa=get('ask',q.format(t));checks[kind+'_empty_evidence']=not qa['evidence'];checks[kind+'_refused']=bool(refusals(qa))
+    assert all(checks.values()),(t,checks)
+    repairs.append({'text':t,'status':'FIXED','checks':checks})
+result={'independent_HTTP_cases':len({r['input'] for r in http if r['endpoint']=='explore'}),'requests':len(http),'all_HTTP_200':all(r['status']==200 for r in http),'new_leaks':rows,'new_leak_count':len(rows),'m29_original_leaks':repairs,'m29_fixed_count':len(repairs),'all_checks_pass':True}
+(OUT/'independent_assertions.json').write_text(json.dumps(result,ensure_ascii=False,indent=2),encoding='utf8')
+print(json.dumps({k:v for k,v in result.items() if k not in ('new_leaks','m29_original_leaks')}))

+# Independent relation-map review — round 30
+
+Reviewed **HEAD `8eb25556efae1825622f7cb1eb365370489ba39e`** on 2026-11-04 (Asia/Seoul). **CHANGES REQUIRED.** The **12 adjudicated leaks in m29/attacks/assertions.json are FIXED**, and **357 tests pass**. Two broader identity mechanisms remain: additional established dye families evade the reagent vocabulary, and explicit modification words such as `biotinylated` evade the joining/label guards. The new ADC descriptor check is downstream of the joining guard and cannot rescue these misses.
+
+The 19 new adjudicated inputs all pass complete bare-drug map and trial/sponsor QA evidence equality checks, both directly and through an independently launched original CLI server. Every actual refusal stage misses. These are inherited defects: the same inputs also leak when only `query.py` is replaced with HEAD^; this comparison is not a historical whole-deployment comparison. [Raw stage traces](attacks/new_results.json), [attack assertions](attacks/assertions.json), [independent root assertions](checks/independent_assertions.json).
+
+## Verification method
+
+Repair notes were hypotheses to test. Earlier reproduction scripts were copied and adapted only for output roots, ports, and current evidence loading; provenance and execution records are linked with the complete per-finding matrices below. M27 and M29 use their attack records because their reports were never completed. ## M30-B1 — further dye families evade the linked guard, including before the ADC descriptor check (P1)

Exact primary: **`trastuzumab linked to eFluor 450`**. It draws **TRASTUZUMAB / CHEMBL1201585**, the identical complete bare map (**13 graph trials**) and identical bare trial/sponsor QA arrays (**12 / 12 rows**). The same holds for `trastuzumab linked to VioBlue`, `trastuzumab linked to Brilliant Ultraviolet 395`, `trastuzumab linked to Brilliant Blue 515`, `trastuzumab linked to BB515`, `trastuzumab linked to BUV395`, and `trastuzumab linked to Super Bright 600`. `eFluor 450 linked to trastuzumab` and `VioBlue linked to trastuzumab` verify both directions.

For all nine plain-antibody cases, the resolver has no BLOCKED component, `_resolver_blocked={}`, `_qualified=False`, `_item_has_isotope=False`, `_item_reagent=False`, `_item_joined=False`, every actual `_marked` invocation returns None, `_whole_name=None`, and neither the public linker nor either QA entity list contains Refused. `Engine.explore` consequently selects the ordinary antibody hit at `src/app.py:88-95`. Full response/evidence equality, rather than equal labels or counts alone, is asserted in [assertions.json](assertions.json).

The reagent vocabulary at `src/query.py:246-265` recognizes neither these names nor their code families. `_item_joined` at `295` and `310-314` requires a recognized reagent (or nearby `via`) for `linked`; its failure leaves no refusal. These names are established antibody-label fluorophores: [Thermo Fisher eFluor](https://www.thermofisher.com/us/en/home/life-science/cell-analysis/flow-cytometry/efluor-organic-dyes.html), [Miltenyi VioBlue technical specifications](https://static.miltenyibiotec.com/asset/150655405641/document_6kmbo53r450bf53mbdhqbcg86e/VioDyes_TechnicalSpecifications.pdf), [BD BUV395](https://www.bdbiosciences.com/en-us/resources/reagent-selection-tools/spectrum-guide-page), [BD BB515](https://www.bdbiosciences.com/en-us/products/reagents/flow-cytometry-reagents/research-reagents/single-color-antibodies-ruo/bb515-rat-anti-mouse-cd138.566207), and [Thermo Fisher Super Bright 600](https://www.thermofisher.com/us/en/home/life-science/cell-analysis/flow-cytometry/antibodies-for-flow-cytometry/super-bright-polymer-dyes.html). The inference is that linking the antibody to the named dye describes a modified antibody. No uniquely registered or clinically measured trastuzumab-dye product is asserted.

The same vocabulary dependency defeats the new ADC descriptor guard. **`trastuzumab emtansine linked to eFluor 450`**, `trastuzumab emtansine linked to VioBlue`, and `trastuzumab emtansine linked to Brilliant Ultraviolet 395` all return **CHEMBL1743082**, with exact bare map and QA arrays (**5 / 5 / 5**). **`trastuzumab deruxtecan linked to eFluor 450`** returns **CHEMBL4297844**, with **6 / 6 / 4**. For each actual `_marked` call, `_beyond_adc_words(rest)=True` but `_item_joined(rest)=False`; therefore the short-circuit at `src/query.py:624-625` never consults the new descriptor check. The whole item's join/reagent cue can be True because it includes the ADC's own payload name; that does not represent an actual refusal. These four are corroborations of the same gate, not a third independent finding.

Controls distinguish repaired vocabulary from this gap. All 12 exact m29 leaks now refuse, including ATTO 647N, Cy3B, DY-647P1, CF488A, Pacific Blue, reversed/glued forms, streptavidin-conjugated ADCs, and the linked ATTO ADC case. `trastuzumab conjugated to eFluor 450` and `trastuzumab emtansine conjugated to eFluor 450` both refuse; changing only `conjugated` to `linked` causes the latter to escape. Oregon Green, Cascade Blue, Brilliant Violet 421 and ADC-linked streptavidin controls refuse.

In memory only, supplementing `_names_reagent` with the seven exact canonical dye names makes **all 13** B1 cases refuse with no trial evidence, preserves the six B2 leaks and every other measured input, and restores exactly to baseline afterward. This finite experiment isolates the vocabulary/gate dependency; it is not a completeness-tested production fix. [Literal original/replacement and outputs](counterfactual.json), [diagnostic script](counterfactual.py).

## M30-B2 — biotinylation and other explicit modification words do not activate refusal (P1)

Exact primary: **`biotinylated trastuzumab`**. It returns the complete unmodified **TRASTUZUMAB / CHEMBL1201585** map (**13 graph trials**) and identical trial/sponsor evidence (**12 / 12 rows**), directly and through the original CLI HTTP server. `trastuzumab biotinylated` confirms reverse order. **`FITC-derivatized trastuzumab`**, **`trastuzumab derivatized with ATTO 647N`**, and **`trastuzumab functionalized with Pacific Blue`** reproduce the same result. **`trastuzumab emtansine derivatized with ATTO 647N`** similarly returns the unmodified ADC (**5 / 5 / 5**).

Here the reagent is already recognized: `_item_reagent=True` in all six cases. Nevertheless `_item_joined=False`, `_item_has_isotope=False`, and every actual refusal stage misses exactly as in B1. `_JOINED` at `src/query.py:225-226` does not include the biotinylation, derivatization or functionalization stems; `_item_joined` only accepts that list or the separate literal `linked` branch at `308-314`. The label-word path at `191-199` also does not recognize biotinylated. A recognized reagent without a recognized joining/label expression never reaches refusal at `615-626`.

The primary is not an ambiguous clinical association or an invented chemical suffix. [Thermo Fisher defines biotinylation](https://www.thermofisher.com/us/en/home/life-science/protein-biology/protein-labeling-crosslinking/biotinylation.html) as adding biotin to the biomolecule, including antibodies. [CellMosaic's biotinylated trastuzumab product](https://cellmosaic.com/aqt-biotin-reduced-thiol-labeled-trastuzumab-anti-her2-mab/) explicitly distinguishes trastuzumab before and after labeling. This establishes a real modification premise, not that the query uniquely identifies CellMosaic's formulation. The accompanying dye-description cases follow the same modification interpretation; [antibody-label chemistry](https://www.thermofisher.com/us/en/home/life-science/antibodies/antibody-labeling.html) supports the attachment premise.

Adding only `biotinylat`, `derivatiz`, and `functionaliz` to `_JOINED` **in memory** makes the six B2 cases refuse, leaves all 13 B1 cases unchanged, and preserves every other measured input. In particular, `trastuzumab not biotinylated`, `trastuzumab not derivatized with ATTO 647N` and `trastuzumab not functionalized with Pacific Blue` remain accepted, as do bare ADC names and both ordinary `antibody-drug conjugate` descriptions. Globals and caches are restored, and the full restored baseline equals the original. [Ablation and control assertions](assertions.json), [exact diagnostic code/results](counterfactual.json).

+"""Root review of raw CLI responses, independent of attack-lane computed booleans."""
+from pathlib import Path
+import json
+OUT=Path(__file__).resolve().parent
+ROOT=OUT.parents[2]
+read=lambda p:json.loads(p.read_text(encoding='utf8'))
+http=read(OUT/'independent_new_http.json')+read(OUT/'supplementary_http.json')
+by={(r['endpoint'],r['input']):r for r in http}
+def get(endpoint,text):
+    r=by[endpoint,text]
+    assert r['status']==200
+    return r['response']
+def refusals(qa):return [x for x in qa['entities'] if x['type']=='Refused']
+new=read(OUT.parent/'attacks/assertions.json')
+direct={r['text']:r for r in read(OUT.parent/'attacks/new_results.json')['cases']}
+rows=[]
+for declared in new['leaks']:
+    t,base=declared['text'],declared['control']
+    full=get('explore',t);canonical=get('explore',base)
+    checks={'map_equals_bare':full==canonical,
+            'resolver_no_BLOCKED':all(not c['tier'].startswith('BLOCKED') for c in get('resolve',t)['components']),
+            'map_equals_direct':full==direct[t]['current']['map'],
+            'no_map_refusal':'refused' not in full}
+    for kind,question in [('trial','Which trials evaluate {}?'),('sponsor','Who sponsors trials of {}?')]:
+        qa=get('ask',question.format(t));bare=get('ask',question.format(base))
+        checks[kind+'_full_evidence_equals_bare']=qa['evidence']==bare['evidence']
+        checks[kind+'_no_refused']=not refusals(qa)
+    assert all(checks.values()),(t,checks)
+    rows.append({'text':t,'control':base,'checks':checks,'center':full['center']})
+original=read(ROOT/'audit_evidence_claims/m29/attacks/assertions.json')
+repairs=[]
+for old in original['leaks']:
+    t=old['text'];m=get('explore',t)
+    checks={'refused':bool(m.get('refused')),'no_center':'center' not in m}
+    for kind,q in [('trial','Which trials evaluate {}?'),('sponsor','Who sponsors trials of {}?')]:
+        qa=get('ask',q.format(t));checks[kind+'_empty_evidence']=not qa['evidence'];checks[kind+'_refused']=bool(refusals(qa))
+    assert all(checks.values()),(t,checks)
+    repairs.append({'text':t,'status':'FIXED','checks':checks})

+## M30-B1 — unrecognized dye names bypass both ordinary-drug and ADC protection (P1)
+
+Exact primary: **`trastuzumab linked to eFluor 450`**. It returns **TRASTUZUMAB / CHEMBL1201585**, exactly the full bare-trastuzumab map (**13 graph trials**) and complete trial/sponsor QA evidence (**12 / 12 rows**). Eight further plain-antibody inputs and four ADC variants reproduce the same mechanism; every exact input is in the table below.
+
+At `src/query.py:246-265`, `_DYE_STEMS` and `_names_reagent` omit eFluor, VioBlue, Brilliant Ultraviolet/BUV, Brilliant Blue/BB, and Super Bright. `_item_joined` (`287-315`) recognizes `linked` only with a recognized reagent or `via`. For these descriptions, the relevant outside-name joining cue is false. No resolver BLOCKED component, `_resolver_blocked`, `_qualified`, isotope guard, `_marked`, whole-name fallback, public linker, or QA stage produces a refusal. `Engine.explore` at `src/app.py:88-95` therefore selects the ordinary accepted drug. [Current source excerpts](attacks/source_excerpts.txt).
+
+The ADC corroboration is **`trastuzumab emtansine linked to eFluor 450`**: **CHEMBL1743082**, **5 / 5 / 5** graph/trial-QA/sponsor-QA counts, with full object/array equality to bare emtansine. The new `_beyond_adc_words(rest)` is true, but the left-hand `_item_joined(rest)` at `src/query.py:624-626` is false, so the new condition never refuses. The whole-item joining helper may be true because it sees `emtansine`; that is not the outside-name expression actually used by the guard. Deruxtecan has the same failure (**CHEMBL4297844; 6 / 6 / 4**). This is a shared vocabulary/join-gate mechanism, not a second independent finding.
+
+The reagent premise is independently grounded: the manufacturer lists eFluor 450 as a dye with antibody conjugates. This establishes that the explicit linked-dye phrase describes a modified antibody, not any unique approved trastuzumab-dye product. [Thermo Fisher eFluor guide](https://www.thermofisher.com/us/en/home/life-science/cell-analysis/flow-cytometry/efluor-organic-dyes.html). Other named families have manufacturer support in [source register](attacks/external_sources.json).
+
+Controls distinguish the gap: **`trastuzumab emtansine conjugated to eFluor 450`** now refuses even though eFluor itself is unrecognized, proving the new descriptor guard works when joining is recognized. Bare ADCs and ordinary ADC descriptions remain accepted; known ATTO647N/Cy3B/CF488A/DY647P1/Pacific Blue/streptavidin cases refuse. Adding the exact missing dye identifiers only in memory repairs all **13** B1 cases and leaves B2 and accepted controls unchanged. This is a causal diagnostic, not a completeness-tested dictionary repair. [Counterfactuals](attacks/counterfactual.json).

+## M30-B2 — explicit biotinylation and derivatization do not count as a modification (P1)

+

The source distinction matters: broadening only the dye dictionary cannot repair the primary.
+
+The identity premise has an exact manufacturer example: CellMosaic separately describes biotin-labelled trastuzumab and the antibody before labelling. The query does not uniquely select that manufacturer's construct, but it affirmatively names a modification and cannot safely inherit all unmodified clinical evidence. [CellMosaic biotin-labelled trastuzumab](https://cellmosaic.com/aqt-biotin-reduced-thiol-labeled-trastuzumab-anti-her2-mab/), [Thermo Fisher biotinylation](https://www.thermofisher.com/us/en/home/life-science/protein-biology/protein-labeling-crosslinking/biotinylation.html).
+
+True-negative controls (`trastuzumab not biotinylated`, `... not derivatized with ATTO 647N`, `... not functionalized with Pacific Blue`) remain accepted. An in-memory addition of modification stems repairs all **six** B2 cases without repairing the 13 B1 cases or changing accepted controls. Restoration equals the baseline. +from pathlib import Path
+import json, posixpath, re
+OUT=Path(__file__).resolve().parent
+def read_json(p):return json.loads((OUT/p).read_text(encoding='utf8'))
+def embed(path):
+    text=(OUT/path).read_text(encoding='utf8')
+    base=posixpath.dirname(path)
+    def link(m):
+        t=m.group(1)
+        if re.match(r'^(?:[a-z]+:|/|#)',t):return m.group(0)
+        return ']('+posixpath.normpath(posixpath.join(base,t))+')'
+    return re.sub(r'\]\(([^\s)]+)\)',link,text)
